searchText: <@892053833121923094> I'm a bit confused about how state tests are supposed to behave when there is no chain_id in the transaction, but there is one in an authorization. It seems they expect to check authorizations against chain_id == 1 in this case, can you confirm? Yes I think this is the way to go, I thought that fixture format had the chain ID somewhere in the environment, but I just checked and this doesn't seem to be the case Hi, Im running the pyspec simulation `./hive --sim ethereum/pyspec --client go-ethereum` and it's failing with `[7b6a7c3e] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`. for every testcase. Am I running the command correctly? Which hive branch are you using? Latest master Yes it's expected, pyspec as is cannot parse the latest fixtures which include prague, <@755913785620824175> <@547171287831805972> I remember there was a branch that fixed this? <@892053833121923094> I'm also confused about `eip7702_set_code_tx/test_set_code_txs.py::test_set_code_using_invalid_signatures` test which cases are valid and which are not? Some cases have `signer` field in authorization alongside `v`, `r`, `s` and some do not, what's the difference and expected test runner behavior? When it doesn't have the signer it means that `v` `r` `s` could not be ec-recovered, and the point is to see how the client behaves with such tx, which is still a valid tx You can try out this branch: https://github.com/spencer-tb/hive/tree/consume-engine We are replacing the `pyspec` simulator for a python port called `consume engine` or the `eest-engine` simulator. It can be run with the following: ``` ./hive --sim ethereum/eest-block-rlp --client go-ethereum --docker.output ``` Hope this helps, and feel free to dm me if there are any issues 😄

excerpts.content:
<@892053833121923094>  I'm also confused about `eip7702_set_code_tx/test_set_code_txs.py::test_set_code_using_invalid_signatures` test
which cases are valid and which are not?
Some cases have `signer` field in authorization alongside `v`, `r`, `s` and some do not, what's the difference and expected test runner behavior?

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: When it doesn't have the signer it means that `v` `r` `s` could not be ec-recovered, and the point is to see how the client behaves with such tx, which is still a valid tx

excerpts.author: spencer_tb
excerpts.content:
You can try out this branch:  https://github.com/spencer-tb/hive/tree/consume-engine
We are replacing the `pyspec` simulator for a python port called `consume engine` or the `eest-engine` simulator. It can be run with the following:
```
./hive --sim ethereum/eest-block-rlp --client go-ethereum --docker.output
```
Hope this helps, and feel free to dm me if there are any issues 😄
